Milwaukee Brewers @ New York Mets, 4:10p

Summary

Jacob Misiorowski is essentially a top-of-the-line watchability lock, and this Brewers-Mets series finale delivers plenty else besides. Misiorowski, in his sophomore season, has been electric, leading MLB in ERA (1.68), strikeouts, and WHIP, and his 100+ mph heat produces the kind of swing-and-miss stuff (elite SwStr%, absurd xFIP-) that fuels his 15.57 pNERD, one of the best you'll see all year. He's opposed by Sean Manaea, a serviceable but unspectacular lefty (4.31 ERA, 4-5) who's been homer-prone this year; his 5.60 pNERD is fine but nowhere near Misiorowski's level. The Brewers own the majors' best record and bring a well-rounded 9.92 tNERD built on baserunning, bullpen depth, and a young roster, while the Mets counter with a middling 5.47 mark, held down by shaky batting and baserunning but boosted by broadcast appeal. Milwaukee already took the series opener 8-1 behind Brice Turang and Sal Frelick, and the finale caps a series that's had playoff-atmosphere intensity despite the Mets' fade from contention. With an 18.28 gNERD score, this ranks near the very top of today's slate and comfortably above the historical average, making it the easy pick if you can only watch one game.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

Both aces looking sharp, both teams fighting for their divisions, and a series that's already delivered two walk-off-flavored nail-biters — this one has the highest gNERD score of the day and it earns it. Yamamoto and Sale rank second and third in the NL in ERA, and Sale carries a pNERD of 10.05 thanks to elite peripherals — a sparkling xFIP- of 65 and strikeout stuff to match. Yamamoto isn't far behind at 7.97, riding a stretch where he's posted a 2.08 ERA while striking out 27 batters across 26 innings in four August starts, and he's dominated Atlanta specifically, with their past two encounters totaling 10 scoreless innings. This is Dodgers-Braves as a legitimate playoff preview: "an August series that has felt more like October baseball," with the Braves already having won the first two games in dramatic fashion, including a walk-off single from seldom-used Ha-Seong Kim. The Dodgers bring the majors' most star-studded, highest-payroll lineup (tNERD 8.26) against a scrappy, barrel-happy Braves offense (tNERD 5.60) that's been unlucky by the numbers and due for better results. With two frontline arms and postseason stakes attached, this is as close to appointment viewing as the day offers.

Baltimore Orioles @ St. Louis Cardinals, 11:15a

Summary

A lopsided pitching matchup wrapped around a series-sweep bid makes this one worth a peek if you like watching one team's plan completely unravel. Trevor Rogers takes the ball for Baltimore riding a hot stretch — he's gone 7-2 with a 2.57 ERA in 14 starts since the start of June, with nine quality starts in that span and only one outing allowing more than three earned runs. His command-over-stuff profile (strong strike rate, modest whiff numbers) checks out with a solid 5.59 pNERD. On the other side, St. Louis is essentially punting the day: the Cardinals are going with a bullpen game, with Gordon Graceffo making his first start of the season and just the second of his career before handing things to relief, meaning his 0.00 pNERD isn't a knock, it's just a lack of a real track record as a starter. The Orioles' offense has been rolling too, having scored 21 runs in the first two games of the series. Team NERDs are middling-to-decent on both sides, with the Cardinals' young, cheap roster and shaky bullpen offsetting Baltimore's barrel-rate pop — solid, not spectacular, gNERD sitting a touch above the historical average.

Houston Astros @ New York Yankees, 4:05p

Summary

Cole in a rubber match against his old team, with the Yankees clinging to a wild-card spot and Houston fighting to stay above .500 — this one has more juice than the raw numbers alone suggest. Cole, at 35, remains one of the game's steadiest forces: he's pitched to a 3.17 xFIP over his last five starts while allowing just a 2.5% barrel rate, and he's held opponents to two barrels over his past 30.2 innings, making it difficult to generate any quick-strike offense. His 96.8 mph average velocity and strong strike-throwing underpin a well-earned 7.73 pNERD, comfortably above the day's average. Wesneski, by contrast, is more modest — his 3.78 pNERD reflects a pitcher who turned in his best start of the season last time out, five shutout innings against Oakland, but he's largely avoided the kind of lineup he'll face here. The Yankees' 7.78 tNERD, fueled by strong barrel and baserunning numbers, dwarfs Houston's punchless 2.83 mark — the Astros' offense has actually been a well below-average unit lately against right-handers. Combine an ace-caliber Cole outing with the Bronx backdrop, and this one's worth a look even if the final gNERD (11.06) sits right around the historical middle.

Arizona Diamondbacks @ San Francisco Giants, 6:45p

Summary

Good enough info to write the summary now.

A middling matchup on paper, livened up by a playoff-hungry Arizona team trying to keep its foot on the gas against a Giants squad with nothing to lose but a real chip on its shoulder. The Diamondbacks arrive winners of five of seven and have throttled San Francisco this year, taking eight of nine meetings, while the Giants are fresh off a series win over the Reds — their first series victory since late July — and would love nothing more than to play spoiler. On the mound, Arizona rolls out rookie Jose Cabrera, recalled for a spot start with an unremarkable line so far 0-2 with a 5.60 ERA and 12 strikeouts in 17 2/3 innings, last seen going 4 1/3 innings against San Diego; no pNERD data exists for him yet, so treat him as a wildcard. Landen Roupp is the more interesting arm, carrying a decent 97 xFIP- and solid strikeout rate, though he's looking to rebound from his current five-start losing skid. Neither team's tNERD impresses — both sit below average, weighed down by shaky Giants baserunning and fielding — so this lands as a below-average watchability day, roughly a 9.99 gNERD against a season mean near 10.8, not urgent viewing unless the division rivalry itself draws you in.

Colorado Rockies @ Washington Nationals, 10:05a

Summary

This one's a slugfest disguised as a pitching matchup, and the pitching won't get in the way. The Rockies own the majors' worst record but have somehow won two straight in this series, while Washington limps in just 2-10 over their last dozen games after getting throttled 13-1 last night. Neither starter inspires much confidence: Gabriel Hughes carries an ugly road split with a 5.10 xFIP on the road compared to a 3.66 xFIP at home, while Jake Irvin has cratered in the second half, posting a 5.55 xFIP, a full run above his first-half mark of 4.19. Fittingly, the ball has been flying all over the field in this series, with the teams averaging 11.3 runs over the first three games — so bring your over/under ticket. The gNERD here (9.09) sits below the historic median and well under today's slate average, dragged down by Colorado's dreadful tNERD (0.96, thanks to bottom-tier batting and barrel rates) even as Washington's offense and baserunning keep their side respectable. Worth a look for chaos, not craft.

Kansas City Royals @ Toronto Blue Jays, 4:07p

Summary

A mid-tier watchability score today, propped up almost entirely by one pitcher's recent hot streak against a Toronto lineup that can't hit water falling out of a boat. Noah Cameron enters with real buzz — he's held opponents scoreless in four of his last six starts and posted a 1.63 ERA in the month of August, and his pNERD of 5.45 (helped by youth and a slow, deliberate pace) reflects a pitcher trending well beyond his peripheral numbers. Across the mound, Spencer Arrighetti is making just his second outing since being acquired from Houston at the deadline, and the early returns aren't pretty — his pNERD sits at a paltry 0.61, dragged down by a bloated xFIP- and shaky command. Both teams' tNERDs are unremarkable, with Kansas City's bullpen (a brutal -2.47 component) and Toronto's barrel-rate/batting woes (-2.01 and -1.30) canceling out any offensive intrigue; Toronto's offense has struggled badly, averaging only 3.94 runs per game, which ranks 30th in MLB. The Royals arrive having just snapped a nine-game winning streak, and Kansas City has some positive-luck upside worth noting, but this is a game whose gNERD of 6.19 sits below today's 11.70 average — watch it for Cameron, not for much else.

Detail

Texas Rangers @ Chicago White Sox, 4:40p

Summary

A pitching duel with real strikeout stuff on both sides makes this one worth your remote. MacKenzie Gore and Sean Burke enter as their respective teams' strikeout leaders—Gore has racked up 750 career strikeouts in 677 innings, while Burke has been a big reason the White Sox have risen up the AL standings, sitting in the top 20 of ERA, WHIP and strikeouts. Both pitchers post nearly identical pNERD marks (6.76 and 6.71) built on similarly stingy xFIP- marks around 90, giving this a nicely symmetrical mound matchup rather than a mismatch. The bigger juice comes from Chicago's tNERD (8.34), fueled by a young, bargain-payroll roster with real pop in the barrel rate—exactly the kind of scrappy, underpaid overachiever profile that makes a lineup fun to watch. Texas checks in lower (5.53) but carries a hefty positive luck score, meaning the Rangers have been underperforming their skill level and are due for better results, even as they've underperformed expectations all season, ranking 25th in runs scored and managing just seven total runs against the Angels. Add it up and you get a gNERD of 13.67, sitting comfortably above the historical average and near the top of today's slate.

entry.content:

Detail

Boston Red Sox @ Miami Marlins, 3:40p

Summary

A near-max gNERD score of 15.64 makes this the day's best watch, anchored by a red-hot Red Sox rookie and two roster-building underdogs. Payton Tolle brings a 9.74 pNERD into a start nearing the one-year anniversary of his debut, and he's been nails lately — he has won four straight decisions and is 2-0 with a 2.16 ERA in four starts this month, backed by elite strike-throwing and whiff rates that outstrip his tidy xFIP-. Miami's mystery starter (probably journeyman Tyler Phillips, who worked out of the bullpen his last time out) carries a blank pNERD, so don't expect fireworks from that side of the mound. Team-wise, the Marlins post the higher tNERD (9.35) thanks to a young, cheap roster and serious positive luck — they're underperforming their skill marks and due for better results. Boston's 7.18 tNERD leans on a strong bullpen and its own modest positive luck. Add in a fresh Rafael Devers subplot back in Boston's lineup, and this one edges out today's average gNERD of 11.48 by a wide margin.

Milwaukee Brewers @ New York Mets, 4:10p

Summary

The best-in-baseball Brewers roll into Citi Field with a live-armed lefty on the mound, and this one's got real gNERD juice. Milwaukee sits at 81-50, MLB's best record, and comes in having taken each of their last three series against the Dodgers, Mariners, and Braves; the Mets, by contrast, own the sixth-worst record in the league and have been outscored by 40 runs this season. Kyle Harrison, whose 10.77 pNERD is well above today's field, has quietly been terrific — his xFIP- of 72 and knack for missing bats and pounding the zone are backed up by real results, including a bounce-back start where he tossed five shutout innings against Seattle, striking out eight in a 22-0 Brewers blowout. He's young (24) and pitches fast, both plusses for watchability. Opposing him is rookie Zac Thornton, who will make his 10th career start after last allowing three earned runs on seven hits in five innings against San Diego — solid enough production, though we don't have advanced metrics to grade him. Milwaukee's tNERD (10.00) is elite, driven by strong baserunning and bullpen work; the Mets are more middling. Overall gNERD of 15.54 ranks near the top of both today's slate and the historical distribution — worth carving out time for.

Pittsburgh Pirates @ San Diego Padres, 6:40p

Summary

Paul Skenes and a Padres bullpen that leads the league in shutting doors — this one has actual stakes and actual talent, even if the box scores haven't been cooperating lately. Skenes still owns elite peripherals (his pNERD of 10.57 is well above today's average), but Pittsburgh needs Skenes to resemble the ace he was in his first two seasons instead of the pitcher who has been pretty mortal lately, and his last outing was shaky — he lasted only 4 1/3 innings and 81 pitches, yielding four hits and three runs with four walks and five strikeouts. King is steadier than flashy, sitting at a modest pNERD of 3.46, but he's been the Padres' most dependable arm this year. San Diego's tNERD (9.93) is buoyed by a shutdown bullpen and strong fielding, both firmly above league norms, while Pittsburgh's solid baserunning gets undercut by shaky defense. The Padres are fighting for their playoff lives, and Monday's extra-inning loss to Pittsburgh only raises the tension. With a gNERD of 15.33 — comfortably above both the historical 95th percentile (15.60 is close) and today's slate average of 11.48 — this is one of the better watches on the board, thanks mostly to Skenes' upside and a Padres club with real October urgency.

entry.content:

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ San Diego Padres, 6:40p

Summary

Ashcraft's electric arm makes this one worth your evening even if Robbie Ray's presence gives you pause. The Pirates' 26-year-old righty enters riding a stretch that got him an All-Star nod as a Misiorowski injury replacement, and he's been nails lately — he beat the Tigers his last time out, allowing one run on five hits while striking out four across eight innings without a walk. His 11.81 pNERD, built on elite strike-throwing and 97-mph heat, is the best pitching mark in today's slate. Ray, by contrast, is scuffling — his below-average strikeout stuff and wandering command produce a middling xFIP and the lowest pNERD on the board, though he's avoided disaster results so far. San Diego brings the juice on the other side of the ball: the Padres have won 14 of their last 18 games and sit tied for the final NL wild card spot, while Pittsburgh has dropped three straight and needs to find something on the road. The Padres' bullpen (headlined by a lights-out closer) and strong glovework push their tNERD near the top of today's games, giving this one a 14.50 gNERD that clears the historical 95th percentile.

Boston Red Sox @ Miami Marlins, 3:40p

Summary

Boston's high-flying offense meets a hot Sandy Alcantara at loanDepot Park, and the tNERD numbers say the "middling" Marlins deserve more respect than their record suggests. Miami actually posts the higher team score here thanks to a young, cheap roster and standout baserunning, while positive luck marks for both sides hint they've been slightly better than their run differentials show. Alcantara has quietly rounded into form — he's averaged roughly 6.54 innings per start this season, and 20.3 outs over his last 15 — and his pNERD gets a real lift from mid-90s-plus velocity that grades near the top of the league. Suarez brings a strong xFIP- and a deliberate pace that plays well on TV, though he's on six days rest after a shaky outing against Arizona where he allowed four earned runs over 5⅓ innings. Notably, Suarez owns a 7-2 record with a 3.07 ERA in 22 career appearances against Miami, giving this some built-in familiarity. With a gNERD of 13.85, comfortably above the day's 11.15 average and solidly in the upper tier historically, this is a legitimately watchable pitching-forward matchup rather than the mismatch the moneyline implies.

Summary

The Cubs bring the NL's best offense to the desert, and Merrill Kelly is the pitcher standing in its way — that's the whole ballgame in one sentence, and it favors turning this one on. Chicago, fresh off a 19-2 blowout of Seattle, arrives with a comfortable wild-card cushion while Arizona sits just outside the field, making every game in this series matter for the Diamondbacks even if it's mostly background noise for the Cubs. Kelly comes in reeling — he gave up six earned runs and allowed seven hits in four innings against the Red Sox — and his 1.56 pNERD reflects an xFIP- north of 120, ugly even by contact-manager standards. Gausman, since being acquired from the Toronto Blue Jays at the trade deadline, is unlucky more than bad — his 6.55 pNERD is buoyed by strong swinging-strike and strike-rate marks plus a healthy luck bump, suggesting better results are coming. The Cubs' 10.66 tNERD is elite, driven by standout fielding and a Pete Crow-Armstrong-powered lineup, while Arizona's offense and broadcast appeal lag. At 12.10, this gNERD sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages — worth a look, particularly for Cubs fans and Kelly's opponents alike.

I have enough to work with now.

Two aces, one pitcher's park, and a real reason to tune in. Zack Wheeler and Logan Gilbert headline this one, and both bring legitimate strikeout stuff into T-Mobile Park, a venue built to smother offense. Kyle Schwarber has been a wrecking ball all season with 39 home runs, while Zack Wheeler's 2.92 ERA makes him one of the more difficult pitchers in the league to solve. Wheeler's peripherals back that up — his xFIP- sits at an excellent 70, and his elite whiff rate drives a pNERD score comfortably above today's average. Gilbert isn't far behind, pairing a 96 mph fastball with strong swing-and-miss numbers, though his plodding pace docks him slightly. Wheeler has 144 strikeouts in 120.1 innings, a 10.8 K/9 rate, so expect quick outs and quiet innings from both dugouts.

The team scores tell a lopsider story, though: Philadelphia's bullpen depth and baserunning give it a solid tNERD, while Seattle's shaky defense drags its number down near replacement level. At 35-30 at home, T-Mobile Park has been a genuine advantage for the Mariners, so don't assume the visitors coast. With a gNERD of 11.89 — above both the historical and today's averages — this game earns its slot on the watch list primarily through pitching craft rather than offensive fireworks; go in expecting a tense, low-scoring affair rather than a slugfest.

Summary

Chase Burns is the reason to tune in here, even if everything else about this game is fighting an uphill battle. The 23-year-old righty is running a 97.7 mph fastball with elite swing-and-miss stuff (xFIP- of 83), and his 10.10 pNERD is comfortably above today's average, making him the single most watchable thing on either roster. Everything else, though, is muted: combined tNERD of 4.04 is well below the historical midpoint, reflecting two teams playing out the string — the Reds are road favorites at -140 over a Giants team that has faded badly and now leans on pitching and ballpark to keep games close. New York Mets @ Chicago White Sox, 11:10a

Summary

I'll proceed with the information gathered from the successful searches.

A rookie sensation with a knee-buckling curveball squares off against a bullpen journeyman having a career revival, on a Chicago South Side surprise team that's quietly become one of baseball's youngest and most fun outfits. This one clears the bar for watchability, and the numbers back up the eyeball test.

Nolan McLean, the Mets' 24-year-old with what scouts already call one of the best curveballs in the league, brings a 7.98 pNERD built on a stingy xFIP- and electric stuff. He had his worst start of the season last time out, surrendering five earned runs over five innings, though he's still pitched to a 3.42 ERA in 24 starts this season. After his midseason call-up to the majors last year, he lit up stuff models en route to a sparkling ERA and WHIP, sitting mid-90s with two fastballs and a curveball that grades as one of the best in the game. Across the mound, Sean Newcomb isn't a household name but posts a respectable 5.61 pNERD, helped by a fast pace and solid contact management, even while absorbing some rough puck. The White Sox, sporting the league's youngest roster and a payroll near the bottom of MLB, still have out-produced expectations at the plate, giving this game a tNERD of 8.74 that dwarfs the Mets' 5.43. With a gNERD of 13.88, well above the historical average and near the top of today's slate, this is one worth carving out time for.

Cristopher Sánchez is having the kind of season that makes an ace's Sunday start must-watch, and this rubber-adjacent finale between two teams still fighting for playoff positioning gives it real stakes on top of the pitching. Sánchez brings a 10.09 pNERD — well above today's average — built on a strikeout-heavy, ground-ball profile that's produced a sparkling xFIP- of 61 and elite swinging-strike and strike rates; he's compiled a 2.51 ERA with 187 strikeouts and has allowed one earned run or fewer in three of his last four starts. Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 4:15p

Summary

This is the best-looking matchup on the board today, full stop. With a gNERD of 18.64 sitting right at the top of today's slate (today's games range from 4.26 to 18.64) and creeping toward the historic ceiling of 20.20, this Pirates-Dodgers tilt pairs two hard-throwing arms with two lineups that can actually hit.

Tarik Skubal takes the ball for LA sporting the best pitcher score of anyone playing today (11.90), built on a microscopic 65 xFIP-, elite swinging-strike and strike rates, and mid-90s-plus stuff that simply doesn't allow hard contact. On the other side, Jared Jones brings his own well-earned intrigue: he returned from internal brace surgery on his UCL, and the images coming back negative meant he'd avoided a serious injury after getting drilled by a comebacker mid-start. His surface numbers have been rocky since returning, a 5.75 ERA over 20.1 innings with a 1.52 WHIP, but his 98.3 mph average velocity and strong peripherals suggest better days are ahead, and his positive luck score backs that up. The Dodgers' loaded offense (tNERD 8.48) against a scrappy, athletic Pirates club that runs well and gets solid bullpen work rounds out a genuinely well-built game worth carving out time for.

Washington Nationals @ Miami Marlins, 1:10p

Summary

Miami's Eury Pérez is must-watch stuff, even if the standings around him mean nothing. The 23-year-old right-hander carries a 15-inning scoreless streak into this one and has been Miami's best story of August, posting a 2.00 ERA through three starts this month, backed by 98 mph heat and elite swing-and-miss stuff that gives him the day's best pNERD score by a mile. Jake Irvin, by contrast, is scuffling — a 2-7 record with a 5.80 ERA and an xFIP- that agrees he's been more hittable than lucky, though positive luck does suggest some correction is overdue. Neither the Nationals (61-69) nor Marlins (65-64) are playing for much beyond pride, but both rosters skew young and cheap, which the tNERD model loves — low payrolls, low ages, and Washington's excellent baserunning and barrel rates offset a genuinely miserable bullpen. Miami's own offense is unspectacular but has overperformed its skills all year. CJ Abrams, already banged up, has historically been overmatched against Pérez. With a gNERD near the top of today's slate, this is one where the pitching matchup carries the appeal even if the standings don't.

Summary

Logan Henderson pitching against a contending Braves lineup is reason enough to tune in, with a scuffling Martín Pérez along for the ride making this look more like a mismatch than a marquee duel. Henderson has been one of the better stories in Milwaukee's rotation this year, and he carries a 2.70 ERA and 3.39 FIP with 75 strikeouts across 63 1/3 innings, having been fantastic in his last outing against the Dodgers, tossing a career-high seven frames on a career-high 93 pitches, allowing one run on three hits and a walk, striking out six. It's also his first career start against Atlanta. His 9.71 pNERD, built on a sharp xFIP- and strong strike-throwing, dwarfs Pérez's modest 3.37, which reflects diminished velocity and shaky command from the 35-year-old journeyman now with his seventh organization. Combine that with Atlanta's respectable 5.43 team mark and you get a gNERD of 14.33, comfortably above both the historical and today's averages — a good bet if you like watching a rising young arm work against a lineup still trying to solve him.

A last-place club visiting a .500ish team isn't the recipe for appointment viewing, and the modest 7.03 gNERD score here backs that up—sitting below the historical average. Detail

Atlanta Braves @ Milwaukee Brewers, 1:10p

Summary

This one has it all: two of the best pitchers in baseball, a real division-race stake, and a preview of a potential October rematch. The gNERD of 20.64 is the top mark of today's slate and among the highest scores in the dataset's history, and once you see the details, it's not hard to see why.

Misiorowski is the headline act, sporting a pNERD of 15.87 that leads the league today, built on a triple-digit fastball (100.7 mph average), a filthy swinging-strike rate, and an xFIP- of 48 that's simply absurd. He's overmatching opponents with a 100-plus mph fastball and a knee-buckling cutter, compiling a big-league-high 210 strikeouts. Across the mound, 37-year-old Sale is no slouch either, still pumping mid-90s heat with elite command, good for a 9.84 pNERD. The pitchers with the major leagues' top two ERAs will go head to head as the NL East-leading Atlanta Braves visit Jacob Misiorowski and the NL Central-leading Milwaukee Brewers, with some suggesting it's quite possibly a pitching preview of Game 1 of an NL Division Series matchup. The Brewers' tNERD of 10.14 is buoyed by strong baserunning and bullpen work, giving this one both star power and team quality — a rare slate-topper worth clearing your schedule for.

Washington Nationals @ Miami Marlins, 4:10p

Summary

Two under-.500 teams with surprisingly lively NERD profiles make this one worth a look, even if the standings suggest otherwise. Washington enters on a skid — the Nationals are trying to avoid losing eight of their last 10 games and have lost five of their last six — while Miami is scuffling too, fresh off being swept by the Phillies in three close games, though the Marlins are technically still in the playoff chase, four games behind the Padres for the final NL Wild Card spot. Both clubs post tNERD scores around 9.1, well above the historic norm, thanks to young rosters, modest payrolls and (for Miami) a Batting Luck score of 1.60 suggesting their offense should be scoring more than it has. On the mound, Brad Lord has been steady all year — a 4.04 ERA, 1.25 WHIP, 8.23 K/9 over 62.1 innings — while Ryan Gusto, still hunting his first win, has quietly turned things around, posting a 3.07 ERA through three starts in August. Neither arm is dominant, but both are solid enough to keep this from turning into a slugfest. With a gNERD of 14.79, well above today's average, this one's worth a spot on the watch list.

Summary

A rookie flamethrower with triple-digit heat takes on a reigning World Series MVP, and the Dodgers' offense makes this one worth the late start. Bubba Chandler, the 23-year-old righty still finding his footing, brings a 98-plus mph fastball and has quietly been effective lately — he's allowed no more than three earned runs in any of his last six starts while turning in a 2.56 ERA and 2.39 FIP. Yamamoto, meanwhile, is riding a stretch where he's coming off 15 strikeouts and one run allowed over his last two starts, and his xFIP- of 81 backs up the shiny surface numbers — he's arguably been a bit unlucky given how well he's actually pitching. The Dodgers' lineup, led by Ohtani and Freeman, pairs with strong fielding and bullpen work to give LA the best team NERD score in this matchup by a wide margin. At a gNERD of 14.33, this sits comfortably above the historical average and season average alike, driven mostly by Yamamoto's excellence and a genuinely dangerous Dodgers roster — worth carving out time for, even against a sub-.500 Pittsburgh club.

Schlittler carries a 10.84 pNERD (well above today's 6.42 average) into a rematch of last week's start, where he brings a 10-6 record and 2.19 ERA into the outing, facing Toronto for the second straight time after allowing one run over 5.1 innings against the Blue Jays on August 15. Ginn brings a decent walk year overall but his stuff metrics (poor strike rate, plodding pace) keep him modest. With Houston's offense recently running cold and Oakland's power surging a bit, expect scoring, but not appointment viewing — this one ranks near the lower half of today's slate and well below the historical average gNERD.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Washington Nationals @ Texas Rangers, 5:05p

Summary

Jacob deGrom takes the mound with genuine intrigue attached: this is a pitcher trying to prove his triceps and hip are cooperating after exiting a start against the Angels a week ago having thrown just two innings before shutting it down. If he's right, watch closely — his stuff still ticks every analytical box, with a 97.3 mph fastball, elite swinging-strike rate, and an xFIP- of 76 that would make pitchers half his age jealous, driving a pNERD of 10.78, comfortably above the day's average. The oft-injured deGrom has a chance to match last season's total of 30 starts, the first time he had reached that number since making 32 in each of his Cy Young Award seasons with the New York Mets in 2018-19. Opposite him, Andrew Alvarez is a perfectly serviceable lefty (pNERD 5.08) without much sizzle — think of him as the seasoning rather than the main course. The Nationals bring real offensive juice, with strong barrel rates and baserunning value pushing their tNERD to 9.17, though a shaky bullpen keeps dragging on their ceiling. The Rangers, by contrast, are a middling, slightly unlucky team (tNERD 4.97) that's gone 3-7 over their last ten. With a gNERD of 15.00 — well above both the historical and today's averages — this one earns its spot near the top of the watch list, deGrom health permitting.

San Francisco Giants @ Cleveland Guardians, 10:10a

Summary

Gavin Williams is having a quietly dominant season, and this is your best excuse of the day to watch a last-place team's road trip. The gNERD score of 14.71 sits comfortably above both the historic 95th percentile (15.60) and today's slate average of 10.50, driven almost entirely by Williams' excellent stuff on the mound.

Williams brings 190 strikeouts and 11 wins, making him one of the more quietly effective starters in the American League, backed by a filthy 70 xFIP- and 97.2 mph average velocity that produce his 12.17 pNERD — comfortably above the 95th percentile line of 10.50. He did get roughed up last time out, allowing five runs in 4 1/3 innings against San Diego, so there's some risk of an early hook. Roupp is respectable if unspectacular (5.54 pNERD), with an 86.3 mph average exit velocity, 29.9% hard-hit rate and 5.1% barrel rate undercut by control issues that have limited him to 5.1 innings per start. On the team side, Cleveland's 7.63 tNERD outpaces San Francisco's 4.09, fueled by a young, cheap roster and a bullpen that's been quietly excellent all year. Neither offense is scary, but with Williams dealing, this one's worth a look.

Seattle Mariners @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

Milwaukee, sitting comfortably atop the NL Central at 78-48, hosts a Mariners club (59-67) whose offense is basically a museum exhibit on how not to score runs — worth tuning in mostly to watch a good team beat up on a bad one, but there's enough pitching intrigue to justify the watch. George Kirby brings the swing-and-miss stuff you want from an ace, sitting at nearly 97 mph with excellent strike-throwing and a tidy xFIP-, and he owns the highest pNERD in this matchup by a clear margin. Robert Gasser, a former Brewer prospect who debuted back in 2024, counters with solid strike-throwing of his own but middling stuff, netting a more modest pNERD. Seattle's offense has been the team's biggest weakness this season, averaging just 3.9 runs per game, 30th in MLB, with a .229 average and .377 slugging — grim reading for Mariners fans. Milwaukee's tNERD of 9.88 is well above the historical 95th percentile, fueled by strong baserunning, bullpen depth, and a young, affordable roster, while Seattle's 3.02 mark reflects real flaws in fielding and baserunning that its offense-only luck (positive, meaning some regression upward may be coming) hasn't offset yet. With a gNERD of 12.51, this sits comfortably above both the historical and today's averages — not a marquee event, but a legitimately watchable pitching duel wrapped around a lopsided team quality gap.

Gerrit Cole against a fading Baltimore rotation is the headline here, with the Yankees looking to complete a series sweep against an Orioles team that's lost three straight. Bradish is a much more middling watch at 2.81 pNERD, with a sluggish pace (21.7s) dragging him down, though he'll make his 25th start with a 3.65 ERA, 8.4 K/9 against 3.9 BB/9, after giving up two earned runs over six innings in his last outing against Tampa Bay. Detail

Chicago White Sox @ Chicago Cubs, 11:20a

Summary

A high-scoring Crosstown Classic finale with real playoff stakes for both sides — this one's worth your remote. With a 14.78 gNERD, this White Sox-Cubs series capper ranks near the top of today's slate and comfortably above the historical average, driven mostly by the Cubs' excellent 10.04 tNERD, fueled by a Sox offense driven by the home run ball, with a lineup built around three sluggers who each have over 25 homers facing off against a Cubs team boasting standout batting and fielding runs. It's worth noting it's rare when both Chicago baseball teams are on track to make the playoffs in August, which gives this series some extra juice. On the mound, Sean Newcomb has been effective out of the White Sox pen and now starts, holding right-handed hitters to just a .194 average this season after tossing 2 1/3 hitless innings against Detroit on Sunday, while Clay Holmes brings a solid xFIP-based pNERD of his own. Neither arm is elite by pNERD standards, but both grade out useful, and the offense-forward Cubs lineup should keep this one lively.

Detroit Tigers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 9:35a

Summary

Paul Skenes remains appointment viewing even when he's not at his absolute best, and that's the whole case for this one. The reigning NL Cy Young winner enters with a pedestrian-for-him 3.88 ERA and has scuffled since late July — a 6.52 ERA over his last four starts, with 20 hits and 11 walks in 19⅓ innings against the Cubs, Reds, Brewers and Marlins — but the underlying stuff hasn't gone anywhere, and his 10.71 pNERD (well above today's 6.05 average) reflects an elite xFIP-, mid-90s velocity, and a whiff rate that still misses bats. Detroit hasn't found answers either; among five healthy Tigers regulars who have faced Skenes, they are a combined 3-for-29 with 2 RBIs. Jackson Jobe, meanwhile, is a total mystery box — no pNERD data available — and his last outing wasn't encouraging, as he struggled in his last outing, chased after 3⅔ innings by the White Sox after allowing nine hits, two homers and six earned runs. Pittsburgh's tNERD (6.58) also outpaces Detroit's (4.26), pushing the 13.27 gNERD comfortably above both the historic and today's averages. Watch for Skenes; don't expect much from the other dugout.

St. Louis Cardinals @ Cincinnati Reds, 3:40p

Summary

Chase Burns is the show here, and the Reds' offense might make sure he doesn't have to be. Burns brings a Cy Young-caliber season into Great American Ball Park — he's 14-2 with a 2.47 ERA in 23 starts, ranked second in the NL in wins and third in ERA and opponents' batting average. He rebounded from a rough Washington start by throwing seven shutout innings with no walks against the Marlins, the first time in his career he'd gone seven scoreless without a walk. His 97.7 mph average velocity and elite whiff rate power a pNERD near the top of today's slate. The opponent is the problem: Cincinnati is buried near the bottom of MLB in batting average and OBP, and had just three hits and one walk in the series opener loss. Liberatore, by contrast, is a league-average arm (5.99 pNERD, 99 xFIP-) getting positive marks mostly for youth and some scuffling luck. St. Louis carries the better team-NERD profile thanks to plus fielding and a young, cheap roster, while Cincinnati's barrel rate and Elly De La Cruz-powered thump provide some counterbalance. At 13.22, this game sits comfortably above the historical average — watch it for Burns, not for offense.

A pitching mismatch masking a genuinely fun watch, thanks to a Nationals team that's quietly one of the more entertaining rosters in baseball. Cade Cavalli, the former top prospect who's finally healthy and pitching like it, takes the mound off a stretch that included carrying a no-hitter into the seventh inning against Chicago, and he brings a tidy 3.46 FIP and 3.36 xFIP that back up his gaudy strikeout numbers — his 7.13 pNERD is well above average. Kumar Rocker, on the other end, is scuffling to a 4-9, 4.50 ERA season with control issues that show up in his below-average strike rate, though he's shown swing-and-miss stuff worth watching develop. Washington's tNERD of 9.08 is the story here — young, athletic, and disruptive on the bases, plus a payroll that says "small market" pretending to be exciting — but the Nats' bullpen (a rough -2.17 component) means Cavalli might not get to finish what he starts. Texas counters with a roster propped up almost entirely by good fortune, a whopping 1.94 luck component suggesting their record is better than the underlying numbers deserve. At 12.57, the gNERD score sits solidly above the historical median and comfortably in today's upper range, making this one of the more watchable matchups on the board despite Washington's four-game skid.

Sasaki still carries the highest pNERD in this matchup, powered by upper-90s velocity and a strong swinging-strike rate, and his underlying skills look better than his 4.46 ERA suggests. He has allowed two or fewer runs in each of his last five starts, and over his last six outings had a 2.50 ERA with 33 strikeouts and 13 walks in 36 innings, and has lasted at least six innings four times. Freeland, by contrast, is a control-over-stuff lefty pitching well below his own home-state fans' expectations — he has a 6.27 ERA in 22 starts, ranking 100th in ERA and 91st in xERA among qualified pitchers. entry.content:

Detroit Tigers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

Braxton Ashcraft alone makes this one worth flipping on, and the Pirates' offense gives it some teeth too. Ashcraft's nine-inning complete game where he allowed one earned run on three hits and three walks while striking out ten just days ago is the headline act here — he needed just 85 pitches to get through all nine innings, averaging less than ten pitches per inning, a feat so rare that only one other pitcher in the 2020s has matched nine innings on 85 or fewer pitches. That start capped an up-and-down season for the 26-year-old, who made his first All-Star team in his first fully healthy season as a starter after battling injuries, though he struggled a bit after the break before this gem. On the team side, Pittsburgh's above-average offense and baserunning nudge this above the daily average, while Detroit's shakier glovework and pen keep the Tigers' tNERD modest. Net-net: watch for Ashcraft, stay for whatever Pittsburgh's lineup can cobble together against Montero.
